keywords.def: the exit point of a letter (plural makharij, مخارج)
the whistle of ص ز س

questions.q: Read «أَوْ يَذَّكَّرُ فَتَنفَعَهُ ٱلذِّكْرَىٰٓ» (80:4) and name the makhraj of each ذ and ك.
questions.a: ذ: tip on the edge of the top teeth; ك: back of the tongue (a little forward of ق).

questions.q: Makharij audit (pupil PDF): for 80:9 to 16, label each tongue letter with its point. Today's rota group recites 80:1 to 8.
questions.a: e.g. ش يَخْشَىٰ middle; ل تَلَهَّىٰ edge to tip; ك كَلَّآ back; ذ تَذْكِرَةٌ tip and top teeth edge; ص صُحُفٍ whistle; ط مُّطَهَّرَةٍ tip and roots; ر بَرَرَةٍ tip with gum.

questions.q: Extend: say three pairs that are often confused and the difference.
questions.a: ث/س: peeps out vs whistle; ذ/ز; ظ/ض: tip vs side.

questions.q: Stretch: why is Arabic called 'the language of the daad'?
questions.a: ض is a sound few other languages have, so Arabic is named after it.

questions.q: Which letter is made with the side of the tongue?
questions.a: A) ض. ض alone is from the side. ظ is the tip on the edge of the top teeth; ط the tip on the roots.
with the tongue tip on the edge of the top teeth
options: with the tongue tip on the edge of the top teeth
with the side of the tongue

questions.q: Think again: The tongue makes 18 of the 28 letters. Why might Allah have given such a small muscle so much work?
questions.a: It is a sign of Allah's design; we thank Him by using the tongue for good speech and His words.
